explanations.answer: Test them to see if they're from God
explanations.explanation: That's the instruction, baker. The writer says, "…do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God." (1 John 4:1) He doesn't tell his readers to panic or to swallow everything whole. He tells them to check. A good baker checks the dough before it goes in the oven, and a good listener checks what he hears.

explanations.answer: Stay far away from every spirit
explanations.explanation: I get the instinct, friend. Keeping your distance from everything can feel safe. But the writer doesn't say to run from every spirit. He says to "…test the spirits to see whether they are from God." (1 John 4:1) Some will pass the test, so he wants them checked, not avoided.

explanations.answer: Trust the one that sounds the kindest
explanations.explanation: Sounding kind is easy, baker. Plenty of things sound sweet and still come out wrong. The writer doesn't give his readers a sweetness test. He says to "…test the spirits to see whether they are from God." (1 John 4:1) A smooth voice doesn't pass the test just for being smooth.

PROPHETS, baker! The writer says, "For many false prophets have gone out into the world." (1 John 4:1) That's his reason for the testing. With that many voices out there, I'd check every one before it got anywhere near my ovens.

Kings is a fair guess, friend, but the word is prophets. The writer says, "For many false prophets have gone out into the world." (1 John 4:1) Prophets are people who speak for God, so false ones are people speaking as if they do. That's why the spirits need testing.

Armies would be a LOT of marching, friend. But the text says something different. The writer says, "For many false prophets have gone out into the world." (1 John 4:1) These are voices, not soldiers, and that's why he wants the spirits tested.

explanations.answer: He has come in the flesh
explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. The writer says, "Every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God…" (1 John 4:2) So the thing to listen for is what a spirit says about Jesus. Confessing that He came in the flesh marks a spirit as from God.

Calling Jesus a great prophet sounds nice, friend, but that isn't the confession the writer names. He says, "Every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God…" (1 John 4:2) The confession he gives is that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh. That's the one to listen for.

explanations.answer: He is an angel from heaven
explanations.explanation: Not this one, friend. The writer says, "Every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God…" (1 John 4:2) The word is flesh. He doesn't mention angels in this verse.

True, baker. The writer says, "…every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God." (1 John 4:3) It comes right after verse 2, where he says, "Every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God…" (1 John 4:2) Read the two verses together and you've got both sides of his test.

Ooh, you came in sniffing for a trap, friend, and I respect that! But this time there's no trap. It's TRUE. The writer says, "…every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God." (1 John 4:3) No maybe, no fine print. Sometimes a card is just a plain sugar cookie with nothing hiding inside.

Already here, baker, back when he wrote it. The writer says it's the spirit of the antichrist, "…which you have heard is coming and which is already in the world at this time." (1 John 4:3) His readers had heard it was coming. He tells them it was already in the world at that time.

explanations.answer: It came and went long ago
explanations.explanation: Not quite, friend. The writer says it's the spirit of the antichrist, "…which you have heard is coming and which is already in the world at this time." (1 John 4:3) He says it's in the world at that time. He doesn't say it's over and done.

That would be a comfy answer, baker, but it's not what the text says. The writer says it's the spirit of the antichrist, "…which you have heard is coming and which is already in the world at this time." (1 John 4:3) Already, he says. Not many years from now.

explanations.answer: Someone greater is in them than in the world
explanations.explanation: That's his reason, baker. The writer says, "…greater is He who is in you than he who is in the world." (1 John 4:4) The overcoming isn't about how clever or how many they are. It's about who is in them, and He is greater.

explanations.answer: They far outnumber the false prophets in the world
explanations.explanation: Numbers sound comforting, friend, but the writer never mentions them. Back in verse 1 he says many false prophets have gone out into the world (1 John 4:1). His reason is this: "…greater is He who is in you than he who is in the world." (1 John 4:4) It's about who is in them.

explanations.answer: They were taught better than the false prophets
explanations.explanation: Good teaching is a fine thing, baker, but that's not the reason he gives. The writer says, "…greater is He who is in you than he who is in the world." (1 John 4:4) His reason is who is in them. He doesn't point to their training.

Careful, friend, this one flips it. The writer says, "They are of the world. That is why they speak from the world’s perspective, and the world listens to them." (1 John 4:5) So the world does listen to them. It's the opposite of what the card said.

False is right, baker. The text says, "They are of the world. That is why they speak from the world’s perspective, and the world listens to them." (1 John 4:5) The world listens to them. The card said it won't, and that's where it went wrong.

True, baker. The writer says, "We are from God. Whoever knows God listens to us…" (1 John 4:6) Knowing God and listening to his side go together in this verse. The verse also says, "whoever is not from God does not listen to us."
It's true, friend. The writer says, "We are from God. Whoever knows God listens to us…" (1 John 4:6) Whoever knows God listens to him, so the card matches the text.
